name: Eric Hassan
home: the blocks north of the port
life: “I left garage work for a year to look after my brother's little boys.” Saturday often includes a stop at the market by Market Flats, where Eric often waits until the delivery baskets are stacked before going in.
voice: I thought the sound came from the old fog bell. That's what my brother told me when I was small.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a brown corduroy jacket and one cuff folded back twice. Eric has one cheek that creases before the other, with black hair twisted into a small knot. Eric counts on the side of one finger where hardly anybody notices during a conversation.
personality: Eric loves an audience until a private hurt enters the room. Then the performer disappears and someone very good at getting other people through a door takes over.
agenda: To ask the brother how the fog-bell story started.
family: Hamish Yeo is Eric’s stepsibling. Eric makes the call. Hamish is free to hang up first. Some of their best calls last less than a minute. A change of tone is sometimes all the news either one needs. Asked about *An empty dedication*, Hamish says, “I paid the electricity through a lean winter.”
connections: Joseph Randall. They compare a sound felt through feet with the old story about a fog bell.
